topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by linking it to previous histopathology practicals and outlining the session's key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Discovery and Experimental Assays of Transforming Oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor-transforming viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and establish the laboratory assays used to evaluate cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated genes and examine their functional and genetic mechanisms using cell cycle regulators and specific mutant proteins as examples.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the distinct forms of sequence and chromosomal instability arising from failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic segregation.

topics.label: Multistep Progression, Hereditary Cancer Predisposition, and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations accelerates cancer progression and drives subsequent tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture, confirms that learning outcomes were met, and suggests supplemental reading for students.
